791731a2 Hidde Beydals <hidde@hhh.computer> | git: worktree, Apply Git's path policy to worktree paths
Some worktree operations use paths from tree diffs or the index without
passing through `ValidTreePath`, such as the deletions of a reset, and
the worktree filesystem checked a `.git` alias only at the first
position. Windows filename rules applied on every host, which refused
POSIX checkouts of names such as `aux.c`.

Check every component in the worktree filesystem as Git's
`verify_path_internal` does [1]: a literal "." or "..", and `.git` in
any case, whatever the configuration says; `core.protectHFS` and
`core.protectNTFS` add the `.git` aliases those filesystems fold, the
8.3 short name `git~1` among them. On Windows, refuse volume prefixes,
and with `core.protectNTFS` the components `Win32ValidPath` refuses, as
Git scopes those rules to Windows [2]. A `.gitmodules` symlink name is
checked first, so callers still get `ErrGitModulesSymlink` when both
rules apply.

Status and Clean list the worktree directly and skip only `.git`. A
name the listing returns is a real file, never `.git`'s short name, so
an untracked directory named like an alias, such as `git~1`, is listed
file by file and removed by Clean, as `git clean -fd` does. go-git
skips `.git` in any case, whatever `core.ignorecase` says, where Git
skips it case-insensitively only under that setting [3]. The difference
is deliberate: on a case-insensitive filesystem `.GIT` may be the
repository's own directory, which would otherwise be listed and
removed by Clean.

Tests compare the gate with the index of a local Git and with POSIX
clones, under every combination of the two settings. `gitAtLeast` now
compares the patch version too, as the protections those comparisons
need shipped in 2.24.1 (CVE-2019-1352, CVE-2019-1353).

The checks this needs are in pathutil.

`WindowsValidPath` omitted the illegal-character checks, so a Windows
worktree could take some repository paths as file streams, and its
reserved-device check missed `LPT0` and a reserved name followed by
spaces. Volume prefixes were found with `filepath.VolumeName`, which
recognises a drive letter on Windows alone.

Refuse colons and the other characters Win32 does not allow, and match
Git's reserved-device check [4]. Add `HasVolumeName`, a host-independent
port of Go's Windows volume-prefix parser [5], with its licence
attribution, so the Windows rules can be tested on any host. Go 1.27
reports no volume name once the candidate holds a ".." component; the
port keeps the Go 1.26 answer and the parity test leaves those inputs
out, as every one of them is refused as a parent directory anyway [6].
Add `IsNTFSDotDot` and `IsNTFSDotCurrent`, the NTFS spellings of ".."
and ".", for the checks that build on them.

Expected results were checked against Git's own validator compiled
locally.

NTFS and HFS+ fold some names back to "." or "..": ".. " and "..:x" on
NTFS, ".<U+200C>." on HFS+, which ignores certain code points. A path
that chroots to such a component, or a storage name below .git built
from one, addresses the directory holding it or the one above, though
`path.Clean` sees an ordinary name.

Add `IsDotOrDotDotName` and `IsDotName`, which match the literal names
and these spellings, and `ValidStorageName`, the check for a submodule's
storage name below .git/modules: not empty, no NUL, no leading or
trailing separator or drive prefix, and no component naming "." or "..",
literally or folded. Git's `check_submodule_name` refuses only an empty
name and a literal ".." [7]; the rest is a deliberate go-git policy,
stricter than Git, that keeps a name from addressing anything but a
directory below .git/modules. A run of periods, such as "...", stays
valid, as in Git. `ValidSubmodulePath` is `ValidTreePath` plus the
folded spellings, for a path that is chrooted into, again stricter than
Git, which does not validate the .gitmodules path. Both apply on every
host, whatever `core.protectHFS` and `core.protectNTFS` say.

`IsHFSDot` returns early for a name that does not start with a period,
as no code point HFS+ ignores is ASCII, so ordinary names are not
converted to runes [8].

`WindowsValidPath` is renamed `Win32ValidPath`, after Git's
`is_valid_win32_path`.

# go-git/go-git#2376 • *: Fix path validation across storage and worktree operations (@hiddeco)

**Outcome:** changes required
All six findings from 2026-10-30 are fixed: the `errLeadingSymlink` rebase, Status/Clean hiding aliases, the rebase onto main, attribution, mode-aware removal (split to #2550), and the exported filter constructor. A differential probe over about 7,500 hostile paths found nothing that head accepts and base rejected, beyond Windows reserved names on POSIX, which matches git. What is left are conformance edges in the new gates.

## Required changes
1. [conformance] Gate the NTFS and HFS parent-alias refusals on `core.protectNTFS` and `core.protectHFS`, as upstream gates its alias checks (internal/pathutil/dotdot.go:19, tree.go:67, worktree_fs.go:266). Introduced. Today `ValidTreePath` and `validPath` refuse `.. `, `..:x` and `.‌.` on every host and setting, so `Tree.Files`, `FindEntry` and checkout fail on POSIX repositories git accepts. `skipPathValidation` is unexported, so there is no opt-out. The periods-only submodule names and dropped `.gitmodules` stanzas (config/modules.go:125, :152) are the same class. upstream: read-cache.c:957-999 (`verify_dotfile` refuses only a literal `..`), submodule-config.c:214-237 and 582-596. git 2.56 `update-index` accepts all three under every protect setting. The PR documents this as policy, but codex agrees disclosure does not settle the conformance impact.
2. [conformance] Don't abort `Clean` on the first untracked `.git` alias (worktree.go:1351, :1365-1375). Partly introduced. `Clean` on `dir/git~1` now fails with `invalid path component` and leaves that entry plus every later untracked file. Main removed nested aliases, and `git clean -fd` removes them all (builtin/clean.c:1071-1078, dir.c:2444).
3. [conformance] Refuse `git~1` only under `core.protectNTFS` (worktree_fs.go:289). Partly introduced. The PR extends the unconditional refusal to the final position (`a/git~1`). git with `core.protectNTFS=false` accepts it (read-cache.c:1027-1034).
4. [conformance] Report an untracked alias directory with a trailing slash, or make `IsUntracked` match entries below it (worktree_status.go:164). Introduced. Status lists `git~1` like a file, so `IsUntracked("git~1/f")` is false. git porcelain prints `?? git~1/`.
5. [other] Use one storage-name check in both `DotGit.Module` and `validSubmoduleName` (storage/filesystem/dotgit/dotgit.go:1912-1917, config/modules.go:148-163). Introduced. The copies already differ: `Module` skips the NUL and drive-prefix checks.
6. [conformance] Fix the `is_valid_win32_path` citations (internal/pathutil/ntfs.go:99, :122, :124, worktree_fs.go:234, :237, and the d95b3c9e message). Introduced. L3155-L3272 is the admin-token/SID code. The function is at L3347-L3469 in v2.54.0.
7. [other] Drop the comment reflows and citation-only churn in `hfs.go` and `ntfs.go`, and fix the stale test comment at worktree_status_test.go:336-342, which says refused names are invisible to Status. Introduced. Codex lists the reflows as an unjustified hunk.

## Optional
- `Validate` returns a bare `ErrModuleBadPath`, which discards which rule fired. This is documented (modules.go:126).
- Commit wording:
  - d68cfcc0 says reference names share the checks now, but it doesn't touch ref validation.
  - 85938bd9 uses the `build:` prefix for a test-only commit.
- The PR title starts with U+2022 (•), and a squash merge would carry it into the subject. There are no zero-width or bidi characters.
- Merge-order hazards:
  - #2384 (`Module`): keep both this PR's pre-checks and #2384's walk.
  - #2372 (worktree_fs.go): don't take its `validPath` doc, which describes the old final-`.git` tolerance.
  - #2550 (worktree_test.go).
- bb6e0c19 fixes #2322 and subsumes #2325. It is also the right fix where #2489 is not: #2489 drops CVE-2019-1353 `.git` alias protection on POSIX and should be closed. Neither is referenced.
- Pre-existing:
  - On Windows, a backslash in an index path is treated as a separator where upstream refuses it.
  - `IsHFSDotGit(".git\xff")` returns false.
  - A multibyte drive letter isn't recognised as a DOS drive prefix.

## Adversarial assessment
**Risk:** low.
- **Differential corpus:** Agent C compared head and base over about 7,500 hostile paths, for every protect setting, on `ValidTreePath`, `validPath`, `validSymlinkName`, `Submodule.Validate` and `DotGit.Module`. The only loosening is Windows reserved names on non-Windows hosts, plus `CON <non-space>` shapes on Windows. Both match upstream. Every `.git`, `git~1`, NTFS/HFS+ and `..` alias that base rejected is still rejected.
- **Mutations:** each of these breaks a test: literal `..` in place of `IsDotOrDotDotName`, Windows-only NTFS alias gating, the HFS fast path skipping names that start with `.`, `Module` without its shape check, and `Submodule.Repository` going back to `ValidTreePath`.
- **NTFS alias protection:** still on for every host by default.
- **HFS fast path:** safe, because every ignorable code point is non-ASCII.
- **85938bd9:** test-only.

**Provenance:** hiddeco, account since 2014, 68 merged PRs. 83910b14 is now authored by Hidde with `Co-authored-by: Sahana Bogar` and both sign-offs. No external dependencies.

## Message to contributor

@hiddeco thanks for looking into this. 🙇

Over about 7,500 hostile paths, the new gates reject everything main rejected. The only names they now accept are Windows reserved names on POSIX, which is what git does, and that fixes #2322 the right way without dropping NTFS `.git` alias protection elsewhere. Every prior item is fixed, including the Sahana attribution. 👏 A few small follow-ups:
- `.. `, `..:x` and `.‌.` are refused by `ValidTreePath` and `validPath` on every host whatever `core.protectNTFS` and `core.protectHFS` say, so `Tree.Files`, `FindEntry` and checkout fail on POSIX repositories git accepts (`verify_dotfile` only refuses a literal `..`). Gating these on the protect settings, like the `.git` aliases, would keep the protection where it matters (dotdot.go:19, worktree_fs.go:266).
- `Clean` on an untracked `dir/git~1` now stops with `invalid path component` and leaves it and every later untracked file behind. Main removed it, and `git clean -fd` removes them all (worktree.go:1351).
- `a/git~1` is now refused even with `core.protectNTFS=false`. Git only refuses it under protectNTFS (worktree_fs.go:289).
- Status lists an alias directory as `git~1` without the trailing slash git prints, so `IsUntracked("git~1/f")` is false (worktree_status.go:164).
- `DotGit.Module` and `validSubmoduleName` each implement the storage-name check, and `Module` already lacks the NUL and drive-prefix checks (dotgit.go:1912).
- the `is_valid_win32_path` links point at mingw.c L3155-L3272, which is the admin-token code. The function is at L3347-L3469 in v2.54.0 (ntfs.go:99).
- the comment reflows in `hfs.go` and `ntfs.go` aren't needed, and the comment at worktree_status_test.go:336 still says refused names are invisible to Status.

- **POSIX:** these are ordinary names.

- **HFS+:** an escape via `.\u200c.` is not demonstrated. Path resolution treats `..` before the filesystem ever compares names.

**Outcome:** changes required
All six findings from 2026-10-30 are fixed: the `errLeadingSymlink` rebase, Status/Clean hiding aliases, the rebase onto main, attribution, mode-aware removal (split to #2550), and the exported filter constructor. A differential probe over about 7,500 hostile paths found nothing that head accepts and base rejected, beyond Windows reserved names on POSIX, which matches git. What is left are conformance edges in the new gates.

## Required changes
1. [conformance] Gate the NTFS and HFS parent-alias refusals on `core.protectNTFS` and `core.protectHFS`, as upstream gates its alias checks (internal/pathutil/dotdot.go:19, tree.go:67, worktree_fs.go:266). Introduced. Today `ValidTreePath` and `validPath` refuse `.. `, `..:x` and `.‌.` on every host and setting, so `Tree.Files`, `FindEntry` and checkout fail on POSIX repositories git accepts. `skipPathValidation` is unexported, so there is no opt-out. The periods-only submodule names and dropped `.gitmodules` stanzas (config/modules.go:125, :152) are the same class. upstream: read-cache.c:957-999 (`verify_dotfile` refuses only a literal `..`), submodule-config.c:214-237 and 582-596. git 2.56 `update-index` accepts all three under every protect setting. The PR documents this as policy, but codex agrees disclosure does not settle the conformance impact.
2. [conformance] Don't abort `Clean` on the first untracked `.git` alias (worktree.go:1351, :1365-1375). 3. [conformance] Refuse `git~1` only under `core.protectNTFS` (worktree_fs.go:289). Partly introduced. The PR extends the unconditional refusal to the final position (`a/git~1`). git with `core.protectNTFS=false` accepts it (read-cache.c:1027-1034).
4. [conformance] Report an untracked alias directory with a trailing slash, or make `IsUntracked` match entries below it (worktree_status.go:164). Introduced. Status lists `git~1` like a file, so `IsUntracked("git~1/f")` is false. git porcelain prints `?? git~1/`.

### Agent C (adversarial)

I found no abuse path in #2376 at ccad2db6, and overall risk is **low**. I compared the head against the range base 91ff528bc473 over about 7,500 hostile path strings. The only thing head accepts that the base rejected is Windows reserved device names (`CON`, `aux.c`, `COM1.`, `NUL:` and so on), and only on non-Windows hosts. Git does the same. Every `.git`, `git~1`, NTFS/HFS+ alias and `..`-alias spelling that the base rejected is still rejected.

**How I checked**
- **Differential probe.** I ran one corpus through both trees and recorded verdicts for `ValidTreePath`, `validPath` and `validSymlinkName` (all four `core.protectNTFS`/`core.protectHFS` settings), `Submodule.Validate` (path and name) and `DotGit.Module`.
  - On the Linux policy, the only loosened rows are reserved names in `validPath` under protectNTFS (2,220 rows). A filter for anything that isn't a reserved name returns 0 rows.
  - On the Windows policy (`win32=true`), the only loosened rows are `CON <non-space>` shapes, such as `CON \u200c`. Upstream `is_valid_win32_path` accepts these too (mingw.c v2.54.0: after the spaces, `c` is not `.`, `:` or a separator, so it goes to `not_a_reserved_name`).
  - Every other column only got stricter: `module` 9,313 rows, `smpath` 4,127, `tree` 375, `validPath` about 400.
- **Mutation tests.** I broke each gate in turn and the tests caught every one:
  - literal `..` in place of `IsDotOrDotDotName` in `validPath`
  - NTFS `.git` aliases gated to Windows only
  - the HFS fast path also skipping names that start with `.`
  - `Module` without its shape check
  - `Submodule.Repository` going back to `ValidTreePath`
- **Test runs.** The PR's tests pass on head with git 2.56.0. I restored the worktree after each mutation and it is clean at ccad2db6.
- **Hidden content.** The diff has no bidi or zero-width characters. The PR body is ASCII apart from the title.

**Your specific questions**
- **`bb6e0c19` (Windows rules only on Windows).** This does not weaken a clone made on Linux and then used on Windows, compared with Git.
  - What NTFS needs protected (`.git`/`git~1` aliases with trailing dots or spaces, `::$INDEX_ALLOCATION`, `.gitmodules` symlink aliases) still applies on every host whenever protectNTFS is on. protectNTFS still defaults to true everywhere (`defaultProtectNTFS`), the same as Git's `PROTECT_NTFS_DEFAULT`.

  - Head now checks volume prefixes on Windows even with protectNTFS off, which is stricter.
- **ASCII fast path in `IsHFSDot`.** It is safe. Every code point HFS+ ignores is non-ASCII, so a name whose first byte is ASCII and not `.` can never match. The mutation test confirms the `.` exception matters.
- **`85938bd9` (git version skip).** This is test-only. `gitAtLeast` now also compares the patch number. The skip only disables the comparison with the local git, and go-git's own assertion still runs (worktree_fs_test.go:661 runs before the `!tc.skipGit` block). The fallback parse is correct.

### Agent C (adversarial)

I found no abuse path in #2376 at ccad2db6, and overall risk is **low**. I compared the head against the range base 91ff528bc473 over about 7,500 hostile path strings. The only thing head accepts that the base rejected is Windows reserved device names (`CON`, `aux.c`, `COM1.`, `NUL:` and so on), and only on non-Windows hosts. Git does the same. Every `.git`, `git~1`, NTFS/HFS+ alias and `..`-alias spelling that the base rejected is still rejected.

**How I checked**
- **Differential probe.** I ran one corpus through both trees and recorded verdicts for `ValidTreePath`, `validPath` and `validSymlinkName` (all four `core.protectNTFS`/`core.protectHFS` settings), `Submodule.Validate` (path and name) and `DotGit.Module`.
  - On the Linux policy, the only loosened rows are reserved names in `validPath` under protectNTFS (2,220 rows). A filter for anything that isn't a reserved name returns 0 rows.
  - On the Windows policy (`win32=true`), the only loosened rows are `CON <non-space>` shapes, such as `CON \u200c`. Upstream `is_valid_win32_path` accepts these too (mingw.c v2.54.0: after the spaces, `c` is not `.`, `:` or a separator, so it goes to `not_a_reserved_name`).
  - Every other column only got stricter: `module` 9,313 rows, `smpath` 4,127, `tree` 375, `validPath` about 400.
- **Mutation tests.** I broke each gate in turn and the tests caught every one:
  - literal `..` in place of `IsDotOrDotDotName` in `validPath`
  - NTFS `.git` aliases gated to Windows only
  - the HFS fast path also skipping names that start with `.`
  - `Module` without its shape check
  - `Submodule.Repository` going back to `ValidTreePath`
- **Test runs.** The PR's tests pass on head with git 2.56.0. I restored the worktree after each mutation and it is clean at ccad2db6.
- **Hidden content.** The diff has no bidi or zero-width characters. The PR body is ASCII apart from the title.

**Your specific questions**
- **`bb6e0c19` (Windows rules only on Windows).** This does not weaken a clone made on Linux and then used on Windows, compared with Git.
  - What NTFS needs protected (`.git`/`git~1` aliases with trailing dots or spaces, `::$INDEX_ALLOCATION`, `.gitmodules` symlink aliases) still applies on every host whenever protectNTFS is on. protectNTFS still defaults to true everywhere (`defaultProtectNTFS`), the same as Git's `PROTECT_NTFS_DEFAULT`.
  - The base never checked trailing dots/spaces or illegal characters off `.git`. Its volume check on Linux did nothing, because `filepath.VolumeName` returns "" there.
  - Head now checks volume prefixes on Windows even with protectNTFS off, which is stricter.
- **ASCII fast path in `IsHFSDot`.** It is safe. Every code point HFS+ ignores is non-ASCII, so a name whose first byte is ASCII and not `.` can never match. The mutation test confirms the `.` exception matters.
- **`85938bd9` (git version skip).** This is test-only. `gitAtLeast` now also compares the patch number. The skip only disables the comparison with the local git, and go-git's own assertion still runs (worktree_fs_test.go:661 runs before the `!tc.skipGit` block). The fallback parse is correct.

**Prior review (2026-10-30)**
- Leading-symlink handling: fixed. `errLeadingSymlink` is handled at worktree.go:1550 and :1563.
- Status/Clean hiding `.git` aliases: fixed. Only the literal `.git` is skipped (worktree.go:1351). Aliases are listed as untracked, and `Clean` fails on them.
- Rebase: fixed. `git merge-tree origin/main HEAD` is clean.
- Attribution: fixed. 83910b14 is authored by Hidde, with `Co-authored-by: Sahana Bogar` and both sign-offs.
- Mode-aware removal: fixed. It moved to #2550, and this PR's worktree.go change is now one comment.
- `NewRootNodeWithDotGitFilter`: fixed. It became the `Options.Opaque` field, which only stops a directory being walked and never hides an entry. The PR body discloses that `Options` can no longer be compared with `==`.
- Wrong mingw.c line citations (C3): still present.

# Review: PR 2266 — reject NTFS and HFS disguised ".." in tree and submodule paths

**Reviewed at** 2026-08-20 iteration 001

**Summary**

Replaces the `dotdotPath` regexp in `config/modules.go` and the literal `".."`
check in `internal/pathutil/tree.go` with `pathutil.IsHFSDot(seg, ".")` /
`IsNTFSDot(seg, ".", "")`, so NTFS (trailing spaces/dots, ADS) and HFS+
(ignorable code points) spellings of `..` are rejected in submodule paths and
tree paths regardless of host OS. Well-scoped hardening with good test
coverage. Verdict: approve.

## Security

This is a security-positive change. It closes a path-traversal class where a
`.gitmodules` path or tree entry disguises `..` using filesystem-specific
folding (`.. `, `..::$INDEX_ALLOCATION`, `.‌.`) that a naive equality or
the old regex missed. The needle semantics are correct:

- `IsHFSDot(seg, ".")` matches `.` + `.` after stripping ignorable code points,
  i.e. `..` and its HFS+ disguises, but not a bare `.` (config/modules.go:50,
  internal/pathutil/tree.go:59). The explicit `part == "."` retained at
  tree.go:59 covers the bare-dot case that the needle form cannot match.
- `IsNTFSDot(seg, ".", "")` with empty `shortnamePrefix` only exercises pattern
  1 (`.` + trailing spaces/periods/ADS); patterns 2 and 3 are gated out by the
  length checks (ntfs.go:132, ntfs.go:141), so there are no false positives
  from the short-name fallback. Verified against ntfs.go:105-171.

## Performance

Negligible. `strings.FieldsFunc` on a submodule path allocates a small slice
per Validate call, replacing a regexp match; for tree paths the per-part check
runs over already-split parts. Both run on validation paths, not hot loops.
Not a concern.

## Go best practices

Consistent with the existing `validSubmoduleName` which already uses
`strings.FieldsFunc(name, isPathSep)` (config/modules.go:147), so reusing
`isPathSep` here is idiomatic. Removing the package-level `regexp` var and its
import is a net simplification. Comments follow the project convention.

Nit: the two-clause comment at config/modules.go:43-48 is long; it reads well
but could be trimmed. Non-blocking.

## Backwards compatibility

Behavior change is strictly a tightening: paths previously accepted that fold to
`..` are now rejected with `ErrModuleBadPath` / `ErrInvalidPath`. The new
`TestValidateGoodPath` confirms legitimate names like `a..b` and `deps/x.y` are
still accepted, so there is no over-rejection of embedded dots. No API surface
change. Acceptable and desirable.

## Blocking issues

None.

## Suggestions

- Consider a test asserting a bare `.` component is still rejected in
  `config` submodule paths too (tree.go keeps the explicit `.` check; modules.go
  relies solely on the needle forms, which do NOT match a lone `.`). A single
  `.` segment in a submodule path is not traversal, but confirm it is intended
  that modules.go no longer flags `.` at all (the old regex did not either).

## Questions for the author

- Was dropping detection of a lone `.` component in submodule `m.Path`
  intentional? The old `dotdotPath` regex only matched `..`, so this is
  unchanged, but worth confirming it aligns with upstream `check_submodule_name`.

func TestCleanKeepsRepositorySpelledInOtherCase(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	dir := t.TempDir()
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "probe"), nil, 0o644))
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "PROBE")); err != nil {
		t.Skip("the filesystem is case-sensitive")
	}
	require.NoError(t, os.Remove(filepath.Join(dir, "probe")))

	_, err := PlainInit(dir, false)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, os.Rename(filepath.Join(dir, ".git"), filepath.Join(dir, ".GIT")))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "untracked"), []byte("x"), 0o644))

	r, err := PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = r.Close() })
	w, err := r.Worktree()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	status, err := w.Status()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, Status{"untracked": &FileStatus{Staging: Untracked, Worktree: Untracked}}, status)

	require.NoError(t, w.Clean(&CleanOptions{Dir: true}))
	_, err = os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, ".GIT", "HEAD"))
	require.NoError(t, err, "Clean removed the repository")
	_, err = os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "untracked"))
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, os.ErrNotExist)
}
